nodes.summary: Titan aims to be among India's top five in safety practices, aspiring to be the safest and healthiest workplace. Its prevention-first safety philosophy emphasizes employee engagement, risk-based audits, and an interdependent approach. The text covers awareness initiatives like the Dare to Care campaign and Project Ve Safe for vendor partners, extensive OSH training reaching over 59,000 individuals with 1.09 lakh man-hours. Jewellery highlights brands Tanishq, Zoya, Mia, and CaratLane, with FY2024-25 revenue of ₹46,571 crore and EBIT of ₹4,764 crore; over 3 million customers, retail expansion, product innovation, franchisee and vendor relationships, tech-led manufacturing including a diamond nano-faceting centre and acid-free refining patent, design process, international expansion, and sustainability initiatives like rainwater harvesting and a Miyawaki forest. nodes.title: Jewellery
nodes.summary: The text covers the Jewellery business segment, highlighting its brands Tanishq, Zoya, Mia, and CaratLane, and their roles in expanding customer reach and delivering curated experiences. It details Tanishq's leadership, Zoya's luxury offerings, Mia's modern edge, and CaratLane's omnichannel accessibility. Financial performance for FY2024-25 is reported: revenue of ₹46,571 crore (21.4% YoY growth) and EBIT of ₹4,764 crore (0.8% YoY growth, 12.1% margin). Jewellery sales surpassed ₹50,000 crore for the first time, with 20% growth, driven by post-duty reduction momentum, festive and wedding demand, and proactive bullion management amid gold price fluctuations.

nodes.title: Growing Meaningful Customer Engagements
nodes.summary: The division maintained steady vision amid economic shifts, gold price changes, and evolving customer preferences, deepening customer connections, reimagining innovation, and expanding in India and beyond. Over 3 million customers purchased jewellery in FY2024-25, with repeat purchases and referrals reflecting trust built on quality, transparent pricing, and personalised experiences. Demand increased for daily-wear lightweight gold and bridal collections, while diamond performance was mixed. 18 karat and investment-focused offerings addressed affordability. The Gold Exchange Programme drove footfall, with over 8 lakh customers exchanging 18+ tonnes of gold. The Rivaah Golden Advantage plan and Golden Harvest offered savings-led purchase planning amid volatile gold prices. A partnership with De Beers promoted natural diamonds via nationwide Diamond Awareness Sessions. Customer feedback was gathered through Net Promoter Scores, brand health tracking, and retail mystery audits.

nodes.summary: The text covers retail network growth through new store openings and enhanced existing stores, emphasizing welcoming design. It details product innovation across brands: Tanishq's collections (Glam-Days, Enchanted Trails, Nav-Raani, Soulmate Diamond Pair, Onam collection, NYFW debut, Rivaah x Tarun Tahiliani), Zoya's Alive and Reborn with patented cuts, and Mia's Firefly targeting younger customers. nodes.title: Growing with Tech-Led Manufacturing
nodes.summary: The text covers the company's tech-led manufacturing advancements: launching a Diamond Nano-Faceting Centre in Mumbai with live demonstrations across 40+ stores; setting up Advanced Gem and Diamond Labs in Mumbai and Jaipur with FTIR microscopes and Raman spectroscopy; filing a patent for the world's first acid-free refining process; winning global recognition including the TPM Excellence Award from the Japan Institute of Plant Maintenance; and establishing a new manufacturing centre in Midnapore for native karigars plus a planned Capability Building Centre for skill development, all reflecting innovation, sustainability, quality, and execution discipline.

nodes.title: Growing by Reimagining Design
nodes.summary:
Growing by Reimagining Design
Our design teams place the consumer at the heart of every product. We conduct market visits to study our own collections and those of our competitors, then enrich these observations with direct interviews and marketing insights. Under the philosophy ‘Design that Inspires’, our TrendLab workshops now convene annually. These workshops bring together designers and business colleagues for deep trend research in areas such as wedding and fast fashion.
Our design process is rooted in a strong narrative shaped by macro trends, setting the tone for every collection. From there, we move swiftly through detailed design and rapid prototyping in close collaboration with our NPI and production teams. Each collection is then refined through cross-functional reviews, ensuring it launches true to intent and ready to connect with our customers.

nodes.title: Growing in New Geographies
nodes.summary: The text highlights Tanishq and Zoya's global expansion into North America and the GCC, positioning Indian jewellery internationally. It discusses the growth of international digital platforms tanishq.com and tanishq.ae as strategic brand and commerce touchpoints, with ongoing investment in functionality, localisation, and omnichannel integration. Marketing strategy is insight-led and AI-driven for personalised campaigns. It also covers sustainability efforts at the Hosur ISCM facility, including two rainwater harvesting cisterns with 1.4 crore litre capacity, reducing groundwater usage by 30% and using 316 lakh litres of rainwater since 2021, with 122 lakh litres in FY24-25, covering 90 days of water needs. Additionally, a Miyawaki forest with 2,800 trees on 60,000 sq ft was created on cistern rooftops.

nodes.title: Making Every Second Memorable
nodes.summary: Titan's Watches & Wearables Division is India's leader, emphasizing innovation, iconic design, and consumer connection. Its brands—Titan for timeless sophistication, Fastrack for bold youth, and Sonata for smart affordability—offer a dynamic range, including smartwatches that empower daily life and health management. For FY2024-25, revenue reached ₹4,576 crore with 17.2% YoY growth, and EBIT was ₹553 crore with 39.3% YoY growth and a 12.1% margin (before exceptional items). The year marked robust double-digit growth across brands, categories, and channels, driven by the core analogue segment. The document includes corporate overview, statutory reports, and financial statements.

nodes.title: Growing through Premiumisation
nodes.summary: The text discusses premiumisation as a growth engine driven by design, aspirational products, and immersive brand experiences. It details brand-specific strategies: Titan elevating horological expertise with Automatics and Stellar Next Edition; Fastrack emphasizing fashion-forward collections like Oceanic, Cosmic Tribe, and Iceberg Automatics; Sonata resonating with Bharat through Sonata Gold and wedding pair watches blending tradition and elegance. In international brands, it focuses on the ₹50,000–₹2.5 lakh premium and bridge-to-luxury segments, enriching the Helios assortment with U-Biot, Charriol, and Herbelin, and accelerating Helios Luxe store rollouts in metro markets. It concludes that premium is an experience, not just a price point, delivered with intent and creativity.

nodes.title: Growing with Product Innovation
nodes.summary: The text highlights product innovation across Titan's brand portfolio, including Titan's first Indian Tourbillon watch in the 40 Years of Joy Commemorative Collection, limited to four pieces at ₹26 lakh and sold out within a month. The Edge range grew 35%, launched Edge Carbon Fibre, became the first Indian brand at the Geneva Watch Grand Prix with two bespoke timepieces, and won the German iF Design Award for Edge Ultraslim. Raga Memoir emphasized storytelling through memory, emotion, and timeless grace. Fastrack launched Fleek, Gambit, and After-Hours, while Titan expanded smart wearables with Celestor and Crown. Sonata refreshed its design language, and Poze and Vyb targeted Gen Z with bold fashion. The report also notes 139 new stores, totaling 1,235.

nodes.title: Growing with Strategic Retail Expansion

Growing with Strategic Retail Expansion
Titan Eye+ is one of the largest mono- brand retail networks under Titan, with over 300 stores nationwide. In Financial Year 2024-25, our expansion efforts were focussed and disciplined. Rather than chasing numbers, we prioritised locations with long-term potential, targeting a net addition of over 50 new stores.
The rising preference for premium international brands reflects a shift in Indian consumer behaviour. To stay ahead, we are curating brand portfolios by catchment, following a multi-brand and multi-segment strategy. While international brands are contributing to value, our in-house brands continue to drive volumes, ensuring a balanced growth trajectory. Our Eyewear business made meaningful progress in international retail, expanding to 7 stores during the year.

nodes.title: Energy
nodes.summary: The Company's total carbon footprint (Scope 1 and 2) is approximately 30,278 tonnes CO2e. It invests in rooftop solar, offset solar and wind power, and energy-efficient technologies to reduce non-renewable energy dependence. A 1MW grid-connected solar plant near Chengam, Tamil Nadu, commissioned in July 2024, supplies the Jewellery Hosur plant, generating 16 lakh units annually and reducing about 1,152 tonnes CO2e per year. At the Jewellery Hosur factory, induction cooking replaced steam-based canteen processes, cutting diesel use by 5,536 litres from FY2023-24 and reducing 14.1 tonnes CO2e annually. At the Watches Hosur plant, an additional 160 kW rooftop solar is expected to generate 2.1 lakh kWh/year and avoid 170 metric tonnes CO2e, plus an energy-efficient chiller was installed. At the EyeCare Chikkballapur factory, lens cutting waste incineration (0.253 kg CO2e per kg waste) was eliminated by converting waste into construction materials like paver blocks and kerb stones for parking areas. Retail stores optimize energy via HVAC monitoring, efficient lighting, and renewable energy. Policies encourage employee EV purchases, significantly increasing EV usage across offices.

The effective interest method is a method of calculating the amortised cost of a financial liability and of allocating interest expense over the relevant period. The effective interest rate is the rate that exactly discounts estimated future cash payments through the expected life of the financial liability, or (where appropriate) a shorter period, to the net carrying amount on initial recognition.

nodes.title: Foreign exchange gains and losses:
nodes.summary:
Foreign exchange gains and losses:
For financial liabilities that are denominated in a foreign currency and are measured at amortised cost at the end of each reporting period, the foreign exchange gains and losses are determined based on the amortised cost of the instruments and are recognised in the statement of consolidated profit and loss. The fair value of financial liabilities denominated in a foreign currency is determined in that foreign currency and translated at the spot rate at the end of the reporting period. For financial liabilities that are measured as at FVTPL, the foreign exchange component forms part of the fair value gains or losses and is recognised in the statement of consolidated profit and loss.

It details administration by the BNRC via a controlled Trust, a maximum of 10,00,000 PSUs, each convertible to one equity share at an exercise price approved by BNRC. It specifies grant by the Board, a three-year vesting period, and a two-year exercise window post-vesting. It notes BNRC's grant of PSUs and the Trust's acquisition of shares from the secondary market. It includes a table showing the movement in options (outstanding, granted, forfeited, exercised) for years ended March 31, 2025, and 2024, and weighted average exercise price per option (₹1).

nodes.title: Fair value measurement
nodes.summary: The text details fair value measurement of options using the Black-Scholes Model, including inputs like exercise price, term, share price, volatility, dividend yield, and risk-free rate. It lists key inputs as of grant date, notes the weighted average remaining contractual life (1.24 years as of 31st March 2025), and estimates fair value using Black-Scholes-Merton assumptions. A table presents data for years ended 31st March 2025 and 2024, covering number of options granted, vesting period (3 years), dividend yield (0.30%), volatility rates, risk-free rates, expected life, weighted average fair value per share, and weighted average share price.

nodes.title: 33.2Shares reserved for issue under Employee Stock Option Scheme
nodes.summary: The text details the CaratLane Stock Option Plan 2017, which supersedes three earlier schemes and allows the Board to grant options vesting over one to four years and exercisable within six years of vesting (or three months after resignation), with a maximum of 7,14,017 options issuable. It provides a movement table of options outstanding, granted, forfeited, converted to cash-settled, exercised, and exercisable for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024, including weighted average exercise prices. A note explains the previous year's Board approval to modify the ESOP plan to a cash-settled plan, including cash payouts, adjustments to retained earnings and ESOP reserves, and fair valuation impacts on the statement of profit and loss for both years, along with details of outstanding, vested, unvested, and forfeited cash-settled options.

nodes.title: i) Relationships
nodes.summary: The text lists related parties of Titan Company Limited, including promoters, associates, key management personnel, group entities, post-employee benefit plan entities, and non-executive directors with their names and relationships. It details related party transactions during the year, such as purchases of property, plant and equipment, other purchases, services, revenue from operations, rent, power and fuel, dividend paid, key managerial personnel compensation, miscellaneous expenses, reimbursements, inter-corporate deposits placed and redeemed, interest and corporate guarantee commission income, miscellaneous income, and contributions to trust funds, with amounts for the current and previous years. It also provides closing balances of outstanding receivables as on the balance sheet date.

nodes.title: Outstanding - payables
nodes.summary: The text presents outstanding payables to related parties of Titan Company Limited for the years ended 31st March 2025 and 31st March 2024, in crore. It lists entities including Tamilnadu Industrial Development Corporation Limited, Tata Sons Private Limited, Tata Consultancy Services Limited, Tata Housing Development Company Limited, Tata Electronics Private Limited, Tata SmartFoodz Limited, Tata Advanced System Limited, TitanX Engine Cooling Inc, Tata Communications Limited, C K Venkataraman, and Others. It specifies relationships as Promoter, Group entity, or KMP. Monetary amounts are provided for both years, with some values in parentheses indicating negative balances. A note states the information is based on available data and relied upon by auditors. The document is from the Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: 35 Financial instruments
nodes.summary: The text presents a financial instruments note with two main categories. For financial assets, it lists items measured at FVTPL and FVTOCI (equity investments and mutual funds) and at amortised cost (trade receivables, cash and cash equivalents, bank balances, inter-corporate deposits, security deposits, non-convertible debentures, government securities, certificate of deposits, employee loans, other loans, lease receivable, other financial assets), plus derivative instruments, with corresponding amounts for March 31, 2025 and 2024. For financial liabilities, it lists items measured at FVTPL (derivative instruments and gold on loan) and at amortised cost (redeemable non-convertible debentures, unsecured and secured term loans from banks, borrowings, trade payables, lease liability, other financial liabilities), plus derivative instruments in designated hedge accounting relationships, with amounts for both dates. It includes totals for each category and appears in consolidated financial statements notes for the year ended March 31, 2025.

nodes.title: 35.2 (i) Fair value hierarchy
nodes.summary: Note 35.2 covers fair value hierarchy, detailing financial assets and liabilities measured at fair value across Level 1, 2, and 3 as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, including quoted investments, unquoted investments, gold on loan, and derivatives. It outlines valuation techniques: quoted market prices for listed instruments, forward exchange rates for FX contracts, bank option prices for currency options, and market comparables or discounted cash flow for others. It states that carrying values of financial assets and liabilities not measured at fair value approximate fair values, reports no transfers between Level 1 and Level 2, and discloses significant unobservable inputs for Level 3 investments using DCF, with sensitivity analysis showing the impact of changes in projected cash flows and discount rates.

nodes.title: 35.3 Financial risk management objective
nodes.summary: The text covers the Group's financial risk management objective, including its Risk Management Committee and framework to identify and evaluate market, credit, and liquidity risks across corporate and business divisions. It details the use of derivative financial instruments for hedging (not speculation) under Board-approved policies. Credit risk management is described, focusing on creditworthy counterparties, collateral, credit norms, and the expected credit loss model under Ind AS 109. Liquidity risk management includes policies for surplus funds, maintaining reserves and facilities, cash flow monitoring, and maturity matching. It provides tables of undrawn funding facilities and contractual maturities of financial liabilities as of March 31, 2025, and 2024.

nodes.title: Credit and Liquidity Risk Management Disclosures
nodes.summary: The page covers credit risk and liquidity risk in notes to consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025. Credit risk section explains the risk of counterparty default, the Group's policy of dealing with creditworthy counterparties, obtaining collateral, managing credit through approved norms, credit limits, continuous monitoring, and using expected credit loss model under Ind AS 109. It notes credit risk arises mainly from receivables and references Note 11.2, while risk on liquid funds, inter-corporate deposits, and derivatives is limited due to high-credit-rated counterparties. Liquidity risk section describes the policy for investing surplus funds in short-term instruments with security and liquidity as primary considerations, and management of liquidity risk through reserves, banking facilities, reserve borrowing facilities, cash flow monitoring, and maturity matching. It also lists undrawn funding facilities: bank overdraft and other facilities of ₹14,097 crore as at 31st March 2025 and ₹10,674 crore as at 31st March 2024.

nodes.title: Liquidity risk tables
nodes.summary: The text presents liquidity risk tables analyzing the Group's financial liabilities by maturity groupings (less than 3 months, 3 to 12 months, and more than 12 months) on an undiscounted basis, based on the earliest payment date. It covers non-derivative liabilities (borrowings, redeemable non-convertible debentures, unsecured and secured term loans, gold on loan, trade payables, lease liability, other financial liabilities) and derivative liabilities (net settled, both in and outside designated hedge accounting relationships). Figures are in crore as at 31st March 2025, with totals for each category, and a note that borrowings exclude interest.

nodes.title: 35.6 Market risk
nodes.summary: The text presents market risk exposure data in crore for March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, broken down by time buckets (less than 3 months, 3 to 12 months, more than 12 months) with totals. It specifies that the Group's market risks are price risk (Note a) and foreign currency risk (Note b).

nodes.title: a) Price risk:
nodes.summary: The text discusses the Group's exposure to gold price risk, including foreign currency fluctuations, and its risk management strategies using derivative financial instruments like future commodity and forward foreign exchange contracts, as well as gold loans. It outlines governance by Board-approved policies, the economic relationship between hedged items and instruments, and details of sell forward/future contracts as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, including average rates, quantities, nominal amounts, and fair values. It also covers fair value hedges, explaining that changes in fair value are recorded in profit and loss, neutralizing profit impact, and presents tables showing hedging instruments and hedged items' carrying values, maturity dates, and balance sheet impacts for both years.

nodes.title: Fair Value Hedge and Commodity Price Risk Disclosures
nodes.summary: The page presents notes to consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025, focusing on derivative instruments used for hedging. It covers the governance of derivative use per Board-approved policies, the economic relationship between hedged items and instruments, and a table of sell forward/future contracts with average rates, quantities, and nominal amounts for 2025 and 2024. It details fair value hedges for gold price risk, including balance sheet line items (other financial assets/liabilities), and states that fair value changes are recorded in profit and loss, neutralizing gold price impact. Commodity price risk tables show carrying values, maturity dates (2-6 months), and fair value impacts for hedged items (fixed gold) and hedging instruments (derivatives) as of both year-ends.

nodes.title: Maturity date
nodes.summary: This text from Titan Company Limited's 2024-25 Annual Report covers notes to consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It details the Group's use of derivative financial instruments governed by Board-approved policies consistent with risk management strategy. It explains the economic relationship between derivatives and hedged items. Tables show sell forward/future contracts for hedges as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, including average rate, quantity, and fair value. Hedging instruments are included in other financial assets and liabilities. Fair value hedges mitigate gold price risk, with changes recorded in profit and loss, eliminating profit impact from gold price fluctuations. Tables present hedging instruments and hedged items positions, including carrying values, maturity dates, and fair value impact on inventories and other financial assets/liabilities for both years.

nodes.title: b) Foreign currency risk management
nodes.summary: Note 35.7 covers foreign currency risk management, detailing the Group's exposure to foreign exchange risk from sales and purchases in various currencies. It outlines risk management strategies for gold purchases/sales (referenced in Note 35.6) and for normal transactions using forward and option contracts measured at fair value through profit and loss. A sensitivity analysis for a 1% increase/decrease in the rupee against major currencies (USD, CHF, EURO, SGD, AED, JPY, HKD, CAD, AUD, GBP) is presented for Titan Company Limited, Titan Engineering & Automation Limited, and CaratLane Trading Private Limited as of March 31, 2025 and 2024. It also lists outstanding forward and option contracts, including 54 USD forward contracts (USD 6.62 crore, ₹565.74 crore), 23 EUR forward contracts (EUR 0.93 crore, ₹84.83 crore), and 3 USD option contracts (USD 0.51 crore, ₹45 crore), with prior year comparatives. Note 36 details inter-corporate deposits (e.g., Bajaj Finance, Tata Realty) with terms and rates, and investments per Section 186, including unquoted equity (Green Infra Wind Power Theni Limited), quoted equity (NELCO, Tata Steel, etc.), other unquoted equity (Innoviti, Great Heights Inc., CueZen Inc., etc.), non-convertible debentures, government securities, and certificate of deposit, showing movements and fair value changes.

nodes.title: Investments
nodes.summary: The text is from Titan Company Limited's Annual Report 2024-25, Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended 31st March 2025. It lists investments by entity name, including quoted equity instruments (NELCO, Tata Steel, Tata Consumer Products, Tata Chemicals, Trent), unquoted equity instruments (Innoviti Payment Solutions, Great Heights Inc., CueZen Inc., Green Infra Wind Generation, Clean Windpower), non-convertible debentures, government securities, and certificates of deposit. For each investment, it specifies the nature of relationship (mostly 'Others'), purpose (wealth creation or strategic investment), and provides a movement schedule in crore showing opening balance, investments made, sold/impaired, foreign exchange fluctuation, and closing balance as of 31st March 2025. A footnote indicates fair valuation movement.

nodes.title: Details of Inter-corporate deposits given and investments made during the previous year:
nodes.summary: The text provides detailed financial data from Titan Company Limited's consolidated statements: inter-corporate deposits with various entities (e.g., Aditya Birla Finance, Bajaj Finance) showing secured/unsecured status, purpose, rates (7.10%-7.90%), terms, and amounts; loans to franchisees/vendors (with a note that none were given during the year); investments in equity and non-convertible debentures (quoted and unquoted) with opening balances, additions, sales, fair value changes, and closing balances; and additional information under Schedule III covering net assets, profit/loss, and other comprehensive income shares for the parent, subsidiaries, and associate, including non-controlling interest and consolidation adjustments.

nodes.title: 38 Capital management
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Group's capital management objectives: maximizing shareholder value, safeguarding business continuity, and supporting growth. Capital requirements are based on annual operating plans and strategic investments, funded through equity, short- and long-term borrowings, and operating cash flows. Gold on loan represents amounts due to banks for gold procurement. The Group aims to manage capital efficiently to continue as a going concern and optimize shareholder returns, with no externally imposed capital requirements. The gross debt-equity ratio is 1.12:1 as of March 31, 2025 (1.08:1 in 2024). Additionally, the Company has a financial covenant for redeemable non-convertible debentures regarding the net debt to EBITDA ratio.

nodes.title: 39 Commercial paper
nodes.summary: The text presents details of commercial paper issued by the Group for the periods ending 31st March 2025 and 2024, including tables showing maturities, face value, and carrying value (e.g., 2-3 months: ₹1,200 crore face value, ₹1,197 crore carrying value in 2025; no balances in 2024). It also includes a movement schedule for commercial paper for both years, covering opening balance, additions, repayments, and closing balance (e.g., opening balance ₹21,262 crore in 2025 vs. ₹62,930 crore in 2024; additions ₹7,431 crore; repayments ₹6,234 crore; closing ₹1,197 crore in 2025; nil in 2024).
